gpu.throttling_title: GPU is throttling — running below rated clocks
gpu.throttling_detail: Reason: {reason}. Your real throughput is lower than the util % suggests — check cooling or the power limit.
gpu.chip_membw_t: Memory-bandwidth utilisation. High here with low GPU util = memory-bound (the usual LLM-inference bottleneck).
gpu.chip_tflops_t: Theoretical peak FP32 throughput at rated boost clock — 2 × {c} shader cores × clock, summed over the cards this tool recognises.{p} It is a ceiling, not a measurement: nothing in the driver reports achieved FLOP/s.
gpu.chip_tflops_now_t: The same peak recomputed at the clock the cards are running at this instant. An idle card parked in a low P-state sits far below its box figure — that gap is the headroom, not a fault.
gpu.chip_tflops16_t: Dense FP16 tensor-core throughput at boost — no sparsity doubling. This is the number that governs LLM inference. Shown only when every recognised card in the box has tensor cores.
gpu.chip_power_t: Draw vs the card power limit. Pinned at ~100% = power-capped.
gpu.chip_pstate_t: P0 = max performance; higher P-numbers = lower clocks.
gpu.chip_perflevel_t: The amdgpu performance policy: auto lets the driver pick clocks, low/high pin them, manual means user-forced levels.
gpu.spill_title: Model spilling into system RAM right now
gpu.spill_past_title: Some model runs spilled into system RAM in this range
gpu.spill_hint: offloaded layers run on the CPU, so generation slows down.
gpu.percard_membw_t: Memory-bandwidth utilisation — high here with low Util = memory-bound

cost.sub_host: · {host}: {parts} measured · no per-process breakdown on remotes yet
cost.rnone_d: Costs need a measured watt source: NVIDIA GPU power (nvidia-smi) or CPU/DRAM via RAPL — which usually needs root to read over SSH. This host reports neither, so there is nothing honest to price.
cost.drill_res_vram: Peak VRAM held {vram} · peak power {peak} W · avg {avg} W
models.empty: No recognised AI model server is running. Start one (Ollama, vLLM, faster-whisper, Stable Diffusion, …) and it will appear here.
models.spill_t: Part of the model does not fit VRAM and sits in system RAM — those layers run on the CPU.
models.now_split_t: {tot} total resident: {vram} in VRAM + {ram} spilled into system RAM
models.wsplit_t: {tot} resident = {w} model weights + {k} context/KV & buffers. Weights are the model file itself; the context/KV part grows with the context window — when weights + context no longer fit free VRAM, the overflow spills into system RAM.
models.runs_t: Load sessions in this range: {g} fully on GPU, {s} spilled into system RAM (worst spill {mb})
models.used_by_t: ~{min}m of connection time to this server while the model was loaded (approximate when models share the server)
registry.title: 📦 Installed models
registry.cap: Every model pulled to this host's local LLM (ollama) — the on-disk inventory, a superset of what's loaded right now. Sizes are on disk; a Loaded badge marks models resident in VRAM this moment. Read-only.
registry.offline_d: Start ollama on this host to list the models pulled to disk. Read-only — the monitor never pulls, loads or removes models.
registry.empty: No models pulled to disk yet. Run "ollama pull <model>" on this host and it will appear here.
models.server_tf_t: The compute this server has under it: {n} card(s){which}, rated peak {f32} TFLOPS FP32{f16}. Specifications, not measurements — no driver reports achieved FLOP/s.
models.server_tf_all: (every card in this box — the host cannot attribute VRAM per card)
models.tf_shared: Shared with any other model loaded on the same server — this is the hardware ceiling, not a per-model allocation.
models.tf_t: {base} TFLOPS {kind} — the rated peak of {where}, which this model is fully resident on. A ceiling from the card specification, not a measurement of work done. {shared}
models.tf_spill_t: {eff} of the {base} TFLOPS {kind} on {where}: only {pct}% of this model is resident in VRAM, and the layers spilled into system RAM run on the CPU, which contributes none of it. Approximate — scaled by bytes resident, and layers differ in cost. {shared}
models.live_serving_t: Scraped live from the server's Prometheus /metrics endpoint
models.no_history: No VRAM history captured for this server in the selected range.
models.spark_cap: Server VRAM — {svc} (shared by all its models) over the selected range

diag.fleet_meta: What the monitor can see on this hub, and how to enable anything that's missing. The dashboard keeps running even when optional pieces aren't mounted — no GPU required.
mcp.card_desc: A read-only MCP server is built in, so Claude — or any MCP client — can connect and explore this homelab with full dashboard parity, right down to what each model and container costs to run.
mcp.connect_hint: Connect with the Claude CLI (then ask it about your fleet):
alerts.intro: Push notifications when something noteworthy happens. Configured here — no env vars, no config files. Any channel (Discord, ntfy, or Telegram) can be used; all are optional. Alerts are edge-triggered (one ping per state change) so they don't spam.
alerts.enabled_label: Alerts enabled — turn the notifier on once a channel below is filled in.
alerts.ntfy_cap: Topic is required; server defaults to https://ntfy.sh. Self-hosted ntfy works too.
alerts.telegram_cap: Required with a bot token. Message your bot once, then read chat.id from getUpdates.
alerts.triggers: Triggers: container unhealthy/exited non-zero/dead, systemd unit failed, GPU VRAM pressure (free < PRESSURE_FREE_MB), GPU OOM events, and disks crossing the threshold above.
costset.intro: Set your electricity price so the dashboard can turn power into money on the 💰 Costs page. Don't know your rates? Pick your country for a typical, editable estimate.
intg.intro: Push run/session data from Jupyter, Colab or Kaggle (or mirror MLflow) — each run comes back priced with the real GPU energy it used. Writes need the API key; the dashboard reads are open on your LAN.
intg.keys_cap: Create one key per machine/notebook so you can track and revoke each independently. Keys are stored hashed — the secret is shown once, at creation.
intg.mlflow_cap: Mirror runs from an MLflow tracking server — they appear under Runs with GPU cost attached. Synced every ~5 min.
backup.intro: Export your SQLite history, events, alert settings, and host registry — or restore a snapshot after a container recreate or disk move. SSH keys under /data/.ssh are not included; back those up separately if needed.
backup.note: Restore replaces all current database contents with the uploaded file. A safety copy of the previous database is kept alongside it as *.pre-restore-*.bak.
hosts.intro: Monitor your other machines from this hub — agentless, read-only, over SSH. Three quick steps: authorize the hub's key on a machine, add it here, then Test.
hosts.step1_t: Authorize this hub on the machine
hosts.step1_d: Run this on the machine you want to monitor so the hub can log in (read-only). Pick its operating system:
hosts.step2_d: A short name and its SSH target. Don't know the address? Scan your LAN for candidates.
hosts.step3_d: Hit Test on a host below — the checklist shows exactly what to fix for anything not yet working, with copy-paste commands for that machine's OS. Typo in a target? Click ✎ to edit it inline.

costs.disabled: Set an electricity price in Settings → Costs to turn power into money.
costs.comp_cap: GPU power is measured (nvidia-smi); CPU/DRAM are measured via RAPL when readable. "Other" appears only if you set a baseline in Settings — wall power is never guessed.
costs.breakdown_cap: Click a row to drill into its power & cost over time. GPU split by VRAM share; CPU split by CPU-time share of the measured package power.
exp.runs_sub: — pushed from your notebooks & MLflow, priced with real GPU energy
exp.runs_empty: No runs yet. Push one from Jupyter/Colab/Kaggle with the tiny client, or wire up MLflow — set it up in Settings → Integrations.
exp.train_sub: — training processes running now (no push needed)
exp.devtools_cap: Auto-discovered DS/AI web tools running on the hub. A 🟡 VRAM tag means a kernel/process is holding GPU memory — often a forgotten notebook squatting on VRAM.
exp.sess_cap: Contiguous GPU-busy periods reconstructed from power & utilisation history — each is a training run, batch job or inference burst. Energy is integrated from GPU power; cost uses your kWh price.
costset.tariff_cap: Powers the 💰 Costs page and the Power & cost cards from power history. Day & Night bills each sample at the night rate inside the window (it may cross midnight) and the day rate otherwise — leave the night price blank to use the single average. Leave the price blank to hide the cost cards.
costset.baseline_cap: GPU and CPU-package power are measured. Wall power is never guessed. Set a flat baseline here only if you want an "Other" band on the Costs chart for the rest of the box.
intg.colab_cap: Colab/Kaggle run in the cloud — point url at a Tailscale/ngrok address that reaches this hub.
net.talkers_cap: Total bytes each container moved over the selected range (its own network namespace).
security.cap: Read-only, agentless — no changes are made to any host. Items shown in grey (⚪) couldn't be read without elevated privileges on that machine.
uptime.title: 🛰️ Uptime checks
uptime.intro: Monitor any HTTP endpoint or TCP port from inside this container — your own services, a NAS, a remote site. No extra uptime service to self-host — it's already here. Down/recovery alerts reuse your configured channels. Targets stay private to this dashboard — they never reach the public status page.
uptime.empty: No checks yet. Add one below — until then nothing is probed (zero outbound traffic).
uptime.f_alerts: Notify me when this goes down and when it recovers (uses your alert channels).
uptime.f_confirm_cap: Anti-flap — a single dropped packet won't page you.
uptime.f_public: Show on the public status page — adds this service to /public (off by default; the page itself stays gated by PUBLIC_STATUS).
uptime.public_t: Listed on the public status page
models.section_cap: One panel per model server: its VRAM timeline (shared by the models it hosts) plus each model's own peak & average. Runs counts contiguous load sessions over the selected range and how many spilled into system RAM (didn't fully fit VRAM — the Now column shows the live VRAM + RAM split). Used by names the apps whose connections to the server overlapped the model's residency — approximate when several models share one server. A server is shown even while Idle (model unloaded / between requests), so nothing vanishes when VRAM is released. Recognised: Ollama, vLLM, SGLang, llama.cpp, LocalAI, HF TGI/TEI, LoRAX, mistral.rs, Aphrodite, koboldcpp, tabbyAPI, text-generation-webui, LM Studio, xinference, OpenLLM, LiteLLM, GPUStack, Cortex/Jan, Ramalama, Nexa, Triton, Infinity, faster-whisper/Speaches, Whisper ASR webservice/WhisperX, Wyoming (HA voice), OpenedAI-Speech, Stable Diffusion (A1111/Forge/SD.Next), InvokeAI, ComfyUI.
footer.about:
Self-hosted & open source • single container • no Prometheus/Grafana required • history downsampled on read. GPU services attributed via /proc/<pid>/cgroup + the Docker API.
Ideas welcome — see CONTRIBUTING.md · issues & PRs always open.
hosts.prefilled: Prefilled — replace "user" with the SSH user, then Add host.
rules.title: 📋 Routing rules
rules.intro: Per-service rules control which channels receive which alerts. If no rule matches, the default (all configured channels) applies. Wildcards (*, ?) work in the pattern column.
registry.empty_host: No models detected on {host} yet. Pull one to ollama there, or start another recognised server, and it will appear here.
gpu.none_cap: The probe found no NVIDIA card (via nvidia-smi) and no AMD or Intel GPU on this host.
gpu.pooled_cap_off: Host offline — showing the last snapshot from {t}
gpu.combined_cap: VRAM stacked per card against the box total, with the hottest card overlaid. Temperature is the maximum across cards, never the average — an average hides the one card that is cooking.
gpu.health_cap: Throttled counts thermal slowdowns only — a card sitting at a deliberately lowered power limit is working as configured, and is reported under Capped instead.
gpu.cards_cap: One panel per card, same rows in the same order and the same scale per metric — so a taller line really is a hotter card. Shaded spans mark thermal throttling. Click a card for the full chart.
gpu.metric_cap: Every card on one axis, so the odd one out is obvious. Shaded spans mark thermal throttling.
gpu.vram_cap_new: Stacked VRAM each service holds on this host, over the selected range.
gpu.attrib_cap: Energy per service is an estimate: each card’s measured draw above its idle floor ({w} W) is shared out in proportion to the VRAM each service holds. GPUs do not meter power per process.
gpu.card_tf_t: Rated peak: {f32} TFLOPS FP32{f16} at {clk} MHz boost, from {cores} shader cores. A specification, not a measurement.
gpu.na_t: This card or driver does not report this metric.
gpu.no_history: No history for this host yet.
gpu.no_history_yet: Collecting per-card history — the first points land within one poll.
gpu.al_gone_d: The card has history on this host but is absent from the latest poll. A card that falls off the bus usually means a driver crash (Xid) or a power/riser fault.
gpu.al_thr_min: GPU {n} has been thermally throttling for {m} min
gpu.al_fanmax: fan already at 100% — no cooling headroom left
gpu.al_hot_d: At or above {h}°C. Not throttling yet{f}.
gpu.al_fanstall: GPU {n} fan is stopped while the card is at {t}°C
gpu.al_fanstall_d: The card reports a fan but it is reading 0%. A seized fan or an unplugged header will cook a GPU under load.
set.gpu_overrides_cap: JSON, host name to °C. A machine whose cards run at a deliberately lowered power limit lives hotter by design — give it its own threshold instead of loosening the whole fleet's.
set.gpu_fanstall: Alert when a fan reads 0% on a warm card
set.gpu_missing: Alert when a card stops reporting
gpu.health_cap_rollup: Over this range the figures come from hourly history, so Hot is rounded to whole hours and Capped is not available.
